addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## npx
NotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).

**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.
**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.
**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.
**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.

Consolidated tools:
- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type
- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type
- studio_revise: Revise individual slides in an existing slide deck
- download_artifact(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Download any artifact type
- note_create/note_list/note_update/note_delete: Manage notes in notebooks

- paseo: Paseo reference for managing agents and worktrees. Load whenever you need to create agents, send them prompts, or manage worktrees.
- paseo-advisor: Spin up a single agent as an advisor — second opinion on the current task. Use when the user says "advisor", "second opinion", "what does X think", or wants an outside take without delegating the work itself.
- paseo-committee: Form a committee of two high-reasoning agents to step back, do root cause analysis, and produce a plan. Use when stuck, looping, tunnel-visioning, or facing a hard planning problem.
- paseo-handoff: Hand off the current task to another agent with full context. Use when the user says "handoff", "hand off", "hand this to", or wants to pass work to another agent.
- paseo-loop: Run an agent loop until an exit condition is met. Use when the user says "loop", "babysit", "keep trying until", "check every X", "watch", or wants iterative autonomous execution.
- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.
- zeroclaw: ZeroClaw Quick Reference
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

aiTitle: Evaluate proto generation for UI from blob schema

content.text:
## Verdict: architecturally correct, producer side is ~80% built, but three blockers sit between the blob and the UI codegen

**What already exists (this surprised me — more than the docs suggest):** every sealed blob carries a valid, typed `google.protobuf.FileDescriptorSet` as a first-class section (`SECTION_DESCRIPTOR_SET`, tag 3, in `crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs:46`). It's synthesized in exactly one place — `crates/op-blob/src/descriptor.rs` — from `PluginSchema.methods`, walking each method's JSON Schema into real typed `Input`/`Output` messages (never `Struct`), with deterministic byte output (name-sorted files and fields) and a hand-rolled wire encoder so the crate stays dependency-free. The catalog can read it zero-copy. So "reflection definition files in the blob" is not a proposal — it's sealed in all 62 live blobs today.

**The pipeline to the UI is cheap.** The UI already uses protobuf-ts, and protoc accepts a pre-built descriptor set directly: `protoc --descriptor_set_in=catalog.bin --ts_out=…`. No `.proto` text reconstruction is needed — export the catalog's concatenated descriptor set to a file, point the existing `proto:gen` script at it, and pin `schema_catalog_hash` into the generated bundle so the UI can detect drift at runtime. That would replace the current state of **three unlinked type sources**: hand-maintained `crates/op-web/ui/proto/*.proto`, hand-written `src/grpc/types/`, and the actual backend schemas.

**Blocker 1 — the typed surface isn't mounted.** `callable_reflection.rs` is explicit: the live gRPC surface is the build.rs-generated `operation.plugin.v1` package where every RPC takes and returns `google.protobuf.Struct`, and the typed `operation.method.*` services "are not mounted here." Generate typed TS clients from the blob descriptors today and they'd call routes that don't exist. Either mount the per-method services or the codegen buys you nothing over the Struct path.

**Blocker 2 — three parallel descriptor generators (the one-schema violation).** Besides op-blob's, `op-grpc-bridge` re-synthesizes descriptors from `PluginSchema` via prost (`per_plugin_reflection.rs::generate_method_file_descriptor_proto`, frozen in `plugin_grpc_gen.rs:147`), and build.rs generates a third set. Per OD-32, nothing reads the blob's sealed section. The bridge should hydrate its reflection catalog from blob section 3 and delete its own synthesis — otherwise UI codegen has two candidate sources and you're back to drift.

**Blocker 3 — OD-32 sealing gaps land first.** Sealing currently drops schema fields (signals, guarantees, etc.), there are two blob-dir writers, and no dir manifest/commit point. Generate UI types from the blob before that's fixed and the UI inherits the truncated schema.

**One design caveat worth internalizing:** the JSON-Schema→proto walk is intentionally lossy — enums, multi-branch unions, and free-form objects degrade to JSON-encoded strings; all integers widen to int64; and no `proto3_optional` flag is emitted, so `Option<scalar>` presence is lost (unset vs `0` are indistinguishable on the wire). That's acceptable for transport but wrong as a form-rendering source. So the split should be: **SCHEMA_JSON (section 1) drives UI rendering** (json_render path — enums, constraints, descriptions survive there), **DESCRIPTOR_SET drives wire typing only**.

Recommended order: (1) bridge reads blob descriptors + mounts typed services, deleting its duplicate synthesis; (2) an `obs.*` export command dumps the catalog descriptor set; (3) repoint `proto:gen` at `--descriptor_set_in`; (4) hash-pin + runtime drift check; (5) delete the hand-maintained protos — including the six for services that should be plugins anyway. Full findings appended to SIGNALS.md under OD-32.

# Requirements — schemars-to-reflection-plugin-pipeline

## Context

Every plugin in `op-dbus` is the single source of truth for its own contract. That contract begins with typed Rust structs, flows through `PluginSchema` (the published interface object), is registered on D-Bus at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`, serialized into `/dev/shm/live-schema.json`, compiled by `build.rs` into gRPC proto services, and exposed through `tonic-reflection` so any client can discover methods without a `.proto` file.

The pipeline works end-to-end today for method inputs. The gaps are:

---

**REQ-3.1** Every schema-level subid (the schema's own OSCAL identifier) MUST be declared on the state struct via `#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.<type>.<subject>.describe@vN"))]`.

**REQ-3.2** Every field-level subid MUST be declared on the struct field via `#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "<category>.<type>.<subject>.<verb>@vN"))]`.

---

**REQ-4.1** Every `MethodDecl` MUST be constructed via `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, Output>(...)`. The deprecated `method_decl_from_schemars::<Input>()` variant MUST NOT be used in new or migrated code.

Create a spec named `phantom-services-to-plugins` (in .kiro/specs/phantom-services-to-plugins/) to eliminate the 6 phantom `operation.<domain>.v1` frontend gRPC services in the op-web UI by wiring the UI to EXISTING plugins through `PluginService.CallMethod` — the only valid path in this architecture. Follow the document structure of the existing spec at .kiro/specs/schemars-to-reflection-plugin-pipeline/ (requirements.md with REQ-N sections, design.md, tasks.md).

## Verified ground truth (2026-07-05 — this OVERRIDES older notes claiming missing backends)

The frontend references six service families that have NO gRPC service anywhere. But every one of the six domains ALREADY has a registered plugin in crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/, sealed as a live blob in /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/, with a typed method surface:

| Phantom frontend service | Existing plugin(s) | Sealed methods |
|---|---|---|
| operation.accountability.v1 ChatbotAccountabilityService | ctl_plane_chatbot | classify_significance, get_episode, list_episodes, query_context, vectorize, get_config, set_config |
| operation.blockchain.v1 BlockchainService | blockchain (blockchain_plugin.rs) | create_snapshot, get_current_state, get_snapshot, get_stats, list_snapshots, rollback, set_retention |
| operation.btrfs.v1 BtrfsService | btrfs (btrfs_plugin.rs) | create_subvolume, delete_subvolume, list_subvolumes, snapshot, balance_start/status, scrub_start/status, device_add/remove, filesystem_df, filesystem_usage |
| operation.agent.persona.v1 PersonaService | persona + agent_config | persona: get_identity, set_identity, authenticate; agent_config: get_config, update_config, reset_config, list_tools, register_tool |
| operation.datastore.v1 DataStoreService | datastore + cozo (+ memory, qdrant) | datastore: list_objects, get_object, query, export, get_stats; cozo: run_query, list_relations, describe_relation, export/import_relations, backup, restore |
| operation.embedding.v1 EmbeddingService | embedding_model (+ qdrant) | embed, list_models, set_model, get_config, update_config; qdrant: search_points, upsert_points, list_collections, ... |

Frontend reality:
- crates/op-web/ui/proto/{blockchain,btrfs,persona,datastore}.proto contain ONLY message definitions — zero `service` blocks. No accountability or embedding proto exists at all.
- Hand-written TS type stubs live at crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/types/{accountability,blockchain,data-stores,persona,embedding}.ts.
- Consuming pages: AccountabilityPage, BtrfsPage, DataStoresPage, KnowledgePage, AgentsPage, EmbeddingPipelinePage, ConfigPage, SecurityPage, GrpcExplorerPage (see crates/op-web/ui/src/pages/).
- Transport: grpc-web via @protobuf-ts in crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/client.ts; PluginService (CallMethod/ListPlugins/GetPluginSchema) is already available there and works end to end.

## Hard architectural constraints (non-negotiable)

1. NEVER create new `operation.<domain>.v1` proto service packages. New backend capability = plugin in crates/op-plugins registered via default_registry.rs. The fix direction is UI→CallMethod, not backend→new services.
2. PluginSchema is the single source of truth: UI request/response types must derive from the plugin schema (blob SCHEMA_JSON section or its gRPC descriptor set), not be hand-written a third time. Args validated against the schema before CallMethod.
3. The sealed blob IS the plugin: existence/capability discovery reads the blob catalog (via ListPlugins/GetPluginSchema surface), never a hardcoded service list.
4. Zero-trust: all calls carry the ghostbridge identity headers already used by client.ts; no new endpoints, no raw ports.
5. No polling/watchers in the UI data layer; reactive fetch on navigation/mutation only.
6. Every new method or surface gets a subid per the taxonomy (categories: src/prj/sch/mut/obs/evt/exp) registered in oscal_subid_registry.rs; mut.* carries actor_id + capability_id.
7. Rust: anyhow/thiserror, simd_json preferred. TS: strict, functional components.

## What the spec must cover

- REQ: a thin typed TS wrapper layer per domain (e.g. src/grpc/plugins/blockchain.ts) that maps page-level calls onto PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id, method, args}, typed from the plugin schema; delete the phantom hand-written types and the service-less proto files they shadow.
- REQ: per-domain method-coverage audit — for each page action, name the plugin method that serves it; genuine gaps become NEW METHODS ON THE EXISTING PLUGIN (with subids), never new services. Flag suspected gaps explicitly as open questions rather than inventing methods.
- REQ: accountability maps to ctl_plane_chatbot; persona/agents pages map to persona + agent_config; stores pages map to datastore + cozo + memory + qdrant; embedding pipeline maps to embedding_model + qdrant. The design must state each page→plugin→method mapping in a table.
- REQ: schema-derived typing strategy: short-term hand-verified TS types are acceptable ONLY if generated/checked against GetPluginSchema at build or test time; long-term alignment with descriptor-set codegen (OD-32) noted as a dependency, not blocking.
- REQ: cleanup — remove dead proto files, dead src/grpc/types/* stubs, and any client.ts references to nonexistent services; GrpcExplorerPage must enumerate from reflection/ListPlugins, not a static list.
- Tasks: incremental per-domain (btrfs first — it is the known simple wiring bug), each task ends with `npx vite build` in crates/op-web/ui green and typecheck green.

Explore the referenced files as needed to write accurate requirements. Do not modify any source code — produce only the spec documents.

content.text:
The BTRFS wiring, in short:

**The bug:** `BtrfsPage` currently calls a phantom `btrfsService` gRPC client (`getSubvolumes`, `getSnapshots`, `getSendState`, `getDrStatus`) that has no backing service on the wire — `crates/op-web/ui/proto/btrfs.proto` only defines *messages*, no `service` block, so these calls were always going to fail/404 at runtime.

**The fix, per the spec:**

1. **Reads** — instead of four separate phantom RPCs, one `StateSync.GetState({ pluginId: "btrfs" })` call (already wired and working in `client.ts`) returns the whole plugin state blob in one shot: `subvolumes`, `snapshots`, `send_state`, `dr_status` are just fields on that state struct. So the four broken calls collapse into a single existing state read — no new backend work needed for reads at all.

2. **Writes/mutations** — `create_subvolume`, `delete_subvolume`, `snapshot`, `balance_start/status`, `scrub_start/status`, `device_add/remove`, `filesystem_df`, `filesystem_usage` are all real methods already registered and sealed on the `btrfs` plugin. These route through the existing, working `PluginService.CallMethod({ pluginId: "btrfs", methodName: "...", arguments, capabilityId })`.

3. **New file**: `src/grpc/plugins/btrfs.ts` — a thin wrapper exposing `btrfsPlugin.listSubvolumes()`, `.getState()`, etc., typed against the btrfs plugin schema, so `BtrfsPage` imports this instead of the phantom service.

4. **Deletions**: the service-less `btrfs.proto`, the phantom `btrfsService` object/types, and its references in `client.ts`/`index.ts`.

It's chosen as Phase 1 (first, before accountability/embedding) precisely because it needs **zero new Rust code** — everything it needs already exists and is sealed in the blob; it's purely a frontend rewiring task, unlike accountability/embedding which need two new plugin methods.

content.text:
Right — I found it. The "blob creator" is the `opblob` CLI (`crates/op-plugins/src/bin/opblob.rs`), and its own header states the pipeline directly: `schema→blob→catalog→btrfs`. It has a dedicated command:

```
opblob btrfs-seal <image> <dir>     seal a catalog dir into a btrfs image
```

That calls `op_blob::btrfs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image()`, whose doc comment confirms your point exactly:

> "The outermost deployment artifact is a btrfs filesystem image whose contents are the sealed plugin object blobs plus an index... mountable (loop/ro), snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able, and self-describing."

Layout: one subvolume per plugin under `/blobs/<plugin_id>/`, sealed via `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink` (no mount, no root needed to build it), then activated later by loop-mounting read-only.

**So the correction to what I told you earlier:** `btrfs_plugin.rs` (the D-Bus-facing plugin `BtrfsPage` should call) is currently a **generic, disconnected** host-btrfs admin surface — `create_subvolume`, `snapshot`, `device_add`, etc. all take arbitrary `path: String` inputs with zero reference to the blob catalog or its image. Meanwhile the actual blob-catalog-btrfs-image logic (`seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image`, `BtrfsImageReport`, `mount_hint`) lives only in `op-blob::btrfs` and is only reachable offline via the `opblob btrfs-seal` CLI — it has no plugin wiring at all.

That means the real intended purpose of the btrfs plugin/page is likely: **surface the blob catalog's own btrfs image** — is it sealed, how big, is it mounted, mount it read-only, or `device_add` it into an existing filesystem to expand capacity — not arbitrary host filesystem admin. Right now those are two unconnected code paths.

This changes the BTRFS phase of the spec: instead of (or in addition to) wiring `BtrfsPage` to the generic `btrfs_plugin`, the plugin itself may need new methods that wrap `op_blob::btrfs` (report image status, trigger `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image`, mount/device_add the blob image) so the UI is managing the actual deployment artifact rather than an arbitrary filesystem path. Want me to update the spec's BTRFS section (REQ-4/design.md) to reflect this, or first confirm with you what `BtrfsPage` is actually supposed to let an operator do?

#### REQ-4.1 — BtrfsPage

**REQ-4.1.0 — Corrected domain purpose (supersedes the generic reading below).**
`btrfs_plugin.rs`'s existing methods (`create_subvolume`, `snapshot`, `device_add`,
`scrub_start`, etc.) are generic, path-based host-btrfs administration — they take
an arbitrary `path: String` and have no awareness of the blob catalog. But the
actual reason a btrfs surface exists in this architecture is `op_blob::btrfs`
(`crates/op-blob/src/btrfs.rs`): the sealed plugin-blob catalog's deployment
artifact IS a btrfs filesystem image (`seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` — one
subvolume per plugin under `/blobs/<plugin_id>/`, built via `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir
--shrink`, mountable read-only/loop, snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able).
Today that logic is reachable **only** offline via the `opblob btrfs-seal <image>
<dir>` CLI command — it has zero plugin/D-Bus wiring, so no live operator surface
can seal, inspect, mount, or `device_add` the blob image into an existing
filesystem for capacity expansion.

`BtrfsPage` MUST therefore expose two conceptually distinct capabilities, not
conflated:

1. **Blob-image lifecycle** (the actual point of this plugin, per
   `docs/BLOB_ARCHITECTURE_SYNTHESIS.md`): seal-status of the current catalog's
   btrfs image (`BtrfsImageReport`: `image_path`, `image_bytes`, `blob_count`,
   `subvolumes`, `mount_hint`), trigger a re-seal, and mount/attach it (loop-mount
   read-only, or `device_add` it into a host array for capacity/redundancy).
2. **Generic host btrfs administration** (subvolumes/snapshots/scrub/balance on
   arbitrary host filesystems) — legitimate but secondary; keep it, but do not let
   it stand in as if it were (1).

| Page action | Plugin | Method | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blob-image status (path, size, blob count, mount hint) | `btrfs` | (OPEN QUESTION BT-2 — new `image_status` method wrapping `op_blob::btrfs::BtrfsImageReport`) | Currently only computable by re-running `btrfs-seal` |
| Seal/reseal blob catalog into image | `btrfs` | (OPEN QUESTION BT-2 — new `seal_image` method wrapping `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image`) | Mutation; needs `mut.*` subid + capability |
| Mount / device_add blob image | `btrfs` | `device_add` (generic) — verify it can target the sealed image path, else new method | See BT-2 |
| Load host subvolumes on mount | `btrfs` | `list_subvolumes` | Generic host btrfs, unrelated to blob image |
| Create subvolume | `btrfs` | `create_subvolume` | Generic |
| Delete subvolume | `btrfs` | `delete_subvolume` | Generic |
| Take snapshot | `btrfs` | `snapshot` | Generic |
| Scrub start | `btrfs` | `scrub_start` | Generic |
| Scrub status | `btrfs` | `scrub_status` | Generic |
| Balance start | `btrfs` | `balance_start` | Generic |
| Balance status | `btrfs` | `balance_status` | Generic |
| Filesystem df | `btrfs` | `filesystem_df` | Generic |
| Filesystem usage | `btrfs` | `filesystem_usage` | Generic |
| Device remove | `btrfs` | `device_remove` | Generic |

**OPEN QUESTION BT-1** (unchanged): The current `BtrfsPage` calls
`btrfsService.getSubvolumes()` (returns subvolumes + RAID info), `getSnapshots()`,
`getSendState()`, and `getDrStatus()`. The `btrfs` plugin's `list_subvolumes`
method takes a `{path}` input. There is no `get_send_state` or `get_dr_status`
method on the `btrfs` plugin. These are either state fields readable via
`GetProperty`/`GetState` on the plugin, or need to be added as new read methods.
Flag for per-method audit in design. Note: `send_state`/`dr_recovery` concepts may
turn out to be blob-image concerns (BT-2) rather than generic-host concerns —
resolve BT-2 first, since it may reframe what BT-1's fields actually mean.

**OPEN QUESTION BT-2** (new): `op_blob::btrfs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` and
`BtrfsImageReport` have no plugin method wrapping them at all — confirm with the
user/design whether `btrfs_plugin.rs` should gain new methods
(`image_status`, `seal_image`, `mount_image`) that call into `op_blob::btrfs`
directly, each with a proper subid (e.g.
`obs.service.btrfs.image-status@v1`, `mut.service.btrfs.image-seal@v1`), before
`BtrfsPage` can present blob-catalog lifecycle rather than only generic host
storage. Do not invent these methods without design sign-off — they cross from
op-plugins into op-blob, a new dependency edge that must be checked for cycles.

`getSendState`, `getDrStatus`. The mapping:

(or `StateSync.GetState` with `pluginId: "btrfs"`) returns the full plugin state
including all these fields. The `BtrfsPage` wrapper should use a single

the fields. This eliminates all four phantom calls in one read. The existing
mutation-side methods (`create_subvolume`, `delete_subvolume`, `snapshot`,
`scrub_start`, etc.) route through `callMethod` as mutations.

New wrapper method:
```ts
async getState(): Promise<BtrfsState> {
  const resp = await stateSync.getState({ pluginId: "btrfs", path: "" });
  return resp.state as BtrfsState;
}
```

`callMethod` — it is a pure state read, not a method invocation.

#### Domain: BTRFS (BtrfsPage)

Plugin: `btrfs` (host-generic admin) **+ new blob-image methods on the same plugin**

**Corrected domain understanding.** `btrfs_plugin.rs`'s `BtrfsState` does have
`subvolumes`, `snapshots`, `send_state`, `dr_status` JSON fields — but they are
hand-rolled **demo/placeholder** values (`@root`/`@home`/`@var` subvolumes, a
fake `root-20260601` snapshot, `active_transfers: 0`) with zero connection to
`op_blob::btrfs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` / `BtrfsImageReport`. The real
btrfs artifact in this system is the blob catalog's own deployment image
(mountable, snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able — see
`docs/BLOB_ARCHITECTURE_SYNTHESIS.md`), currently sealable **only** offline via
`opblob btrfs-seal <image> <dir>`. So resolving BT-1 by wiring `GetState` alone
would surface fake data as if it were live blob-image status — that is worse
than the phantom-service bug it replaces.

**Two-track resolution:**

**Track A — generic host btrfs (existing methods, safe to wire as-is):**

| Phantom call | Plugin method | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Create/delete/snapshot/scrub/balance/df/usage/device ops | `create_subvolume`, `delete_subvolume`, `snapshot`, `scrub_start`, `scrub_status`, `balance_start`, `balance_status`, `filesystem_df`, `filesystem_usage`, `device_add`, `device_remove` | Route through `callMethod` as mutations/reads, unchanged from the original mapping |

**Track B — blob-image lifecycle (OPEN QUESTION BT-2, needs new plugin methods):**

| Page need | Proposed new method | subid |
|---|---|---|
| Blob-image status (path, bytes, blob_count, mount_hint) | `image_status` on `btrfs` plugin, wrapping `BtrfsImageReport` | `obs.service.btrfs.image-status@v1` |
| Seal/reseal blob catalog → btrfs image | `seal_image` on `btrfs` plugin, wrapping `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` | `mut.service.btrfs.image-seal@v1` |
| Mount / device_add the sealed image into a host array | reuse `device_add` if it can target the image path directly, else `mount_image` | `mut.service.btrfs.image-mount@v1` |

Track B requires `op-plugins` to depend on `op-blob` (check for a dependency
cycle — `op-blob` currently has no dependency back on `op-plugins`, so this
should be a clean one-directional edge, but confirm before implementing).

**Resolution of OPEN BT-1** (Track A only, scoped down from the original
all-four-fields claim): `getSubvolumes()` maps to `list_subvolumes({ path })`
directly. `getSnapshots()`, `getSendState()`, `getDrStatus()` should NOT be
satisfied by reading `BtrfsState`'s demo fields — until Track B lands, the page
should either omit these panels or clearly label them as host-generic
placeholders, not blob-catalog DR/send status.

Track A wrapper (unaffected by BT-2):
```ts
async listSubvolumes(path: string): Promise<ListSubvolumesOutput> {
  const resp = await pluginService.callMethod({
    pluginId: "btrfs", methodName: "list_subvolumes",
    arguments: [{ structValue: { fields: { path: { stringValue: path } } } }],
    actorId: "", capabilityId: "cap.storage.btrfs.subvolume.list@v1",
  });
  return unwrap<ListSubvolumesOutput>(resp);
}
```

Track B wrapper (blocked on BT-2 design sign-off and new Rust methods):
```ts
async getImageStatus(): Promise<BtrfsImageStatus> {
  const resp = await pluginService.callMethod({
    pluginId: "btrfs", methodName: "image_status",
    arguments: [], actorId: "", capabilityId: "cap.storage.btrfs.image.status@v1",
  });
  return unwrap<BtrfsImageStatus>(resp);
}
```

blob-catalog btrfs deployment image, currently sealable only offline via

1. Should `btrfs_plugin.rs` (op-plugins) take a dependency on `op-blob` to call
   `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image`/read `BtrfsImageReport` directly? Check for a
   dependency cycle first (`cargo tree -p op-blob -i op-plugins` should be empty).
2. Should sealing/mounting stay an operator-triggered offline `opblob` step, with
   the plugin only exposing read-only `image_status`, or should the UI be able to
   trigger `seal_image` live?

unresolved, proceed with Tasks 1.1–1.3 (Track A only) and leave BT-2 open.

resolve `getSnapshots`/`getSendState`/`getDrStatus` by reading
`BtrfsState`'s demo fields — that would surface placeholder data as if it were
real blob-image status. Only `getSubvolumes()` has a genuine live-data
replacement (`list_subvolumes`). The other three stay unwired (or return an
explicit "not yet available" state) until BT-2 is resolved.

     `ScrubStartInput`, `ScrubStatusInput`, `BalanceStartInput`, `BalanceStatusInput`,
     `FilesystemDfInput`, `FilesystemUsageInput`, `DeviceAddInput`, `DeviceRemoveInput`.
   - Verify field names against `btrfs_plugin.rs` method input structs (not
     `BtrfsState` — that struct is demo data, not a schema to build the wrapper
     against).

     `createSubvolume`, `deleteSubvolume`, `snapshot`, `scrubStart`, `scrubStatus`,
     `balanceStart`, `balanceStatus`, `filesystemDf`, `filesystemUsage`,
     `deviceAdd`, `deviceRemove`. All route through `pluginService.callMethod`
     with `pluginId: "btrfs"`, the method's `methodName`, and its
     `capabilityId`.

     plugin yet — see Task 1.0/BT-2.

btrfs artifact in this system is the blob catalog's own deployment image
(mountable, snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able — see

would surface fake data as if it were live blob-image status — that is worse

| Phantom call | Plugin method | Notes |
|---|---|---|

1	# Tasks — phantom-services-to-plugins
2	
3	Each task is self-contained and ends with `npx vite build` green and typecheck
4	green in `crates/op-web/ui`. Tasks are ordered by risk (simplest first) but are
5	otherwise independent — any domain can be paused without blocking others.

9	## Phase 0 — Shared Infrastructure
10	
11	### Task 0.1 — Create `src/grpc/plugins/` Directory and Utility Module
12	
13	**Requirements**: REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, NFR-2
14	
15	**Context**: The six wrapper files share a small `unwrap<T>` helper and an
16	`argsFromObject` encoder. Centralising these prevents per-file drift.
17	
18	**Steps**:
19	1. Create `crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/plugins/` directory.
20	2. Create `crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/plugins/_util.ts`:
21	   ```ts
22	   import type { CallMethodResponse } from "@/grpc/types/plugin-service";
23	   import type { ProtobufValue } from "@/grpc/google/protobuf/struct";
24	
25	   /** Unwrap a successful CallMethodResponse or throw with the server error message. */
26	   export function unwrap<T>(resp: CallMethodResponse): T {
27	     if (!resp.success) {
28	       throw new Error(resp.error?.message ?? "Plugin call failed");
29	     }
30	     if (!resp.result) {
31	       return {} as T;
32	     }
33	     const v = resp.result as Record<string, unknown>;
34	     return (v["structValue"] ?? v) as T;
35	   }
36	
37	   /** Convert a plain JS object to a single-element ProtobufValue args array. */
38	   export function argsFromObject(obj: Record<string, unknown>): ProtobufValue[] {
39	     if (Object.keys(obj).length === 0) return [];
40	     return [{ structValue: objectToFields(obj) } as ProtobufValue];
41	   }
42	
43	   function objectToFields(obj: Record<string, unknown>): { fields: Record<string, ProtobufValue> } {
44	     const fields: Record<string, ProtobufValue> = {};
45	     for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj)) {
46	       fields[k] = jsToProtoValue(v);
47	     }
48	     return { fields };
49	   }
50	
51	   function jsToProtoValue(v: unknown): ProtobufValue {
52	     if (v === null || v === undefined) return { nullValue: 0 } as ProtobufValue;
53	     if (typeof v === "boolean") return { boolValue: v } as ProtobufValue;
54	     if (typeof v === "number") return { numberValue: v } as ProtobufValue;
55	     if (typeof v === "string") return { stringValue: v } as ProtobufValue;
56	     if (Array.isArray(v)) return { listValue: { values: v.map(jsToProtoValue) } } as ProtobufValue;
57	     if (typeof v === "object") return { structValue: objectToFields(v as Record<string, unknown>) } as ProtobufValue;
58	     return { stringValue: String(v) } as ProtobufValue;
59	   }
60	   ```
61	3. Run `npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui` — green (no pages changed yet).

# Tasks — phantom-services-to-plugins

Each task is self-contained and ends with `npx vite build` green and typecheck
green in `crates/op-web/ui`. Tasks are ordered by risk (simplest first) but are
otherwise independent — any domain can be paused without blocking others.

---

## Phase 0 — Shared Infrastructure

### Task 0.1 — Create `src/grpc/plugins/` Directory and Utility Module

**Requirements**: REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, NFR-2

**Context**: The six wrapper files share a small `unwrap<T>` helper and an
`argsFromObject` encoder. Centralising these prevents per-file drift.

**Steps**:
1. Create `crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/plugins/` directory.
2. Create `crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/plugins/_util.ts`:
   ```ts
   import type { CallMethodResponse } from "@/grpc/types/plugin-service";
   import type { ProtobufValue } from "@/grpc/google/protobuf/struct";

   /** Unwrap a successful CallMethodResponse or throw with the server error message. */
   export function unwrap<T>(resp: CallMethodResponse): T {
     if (!resp.success) {
       throw new Error(resp.error?.message ?? "Plugin call failed");
     }
     if (!resp.result) {
       return {} as T;
     }
     const v = resp.result as Record<string, unknown>;
     return (v["structValue"] ?? v) as T;
   }

   /** Convert a plain JS object to a single-element ProtobufValue args array. */
   export function argsFromObject(obj: Record<string, unknown>): ProtobufValue[] {
     if (Object.keys(obj).length === 0) return [];
     return [{ structValue: objectToFields(obj) } as ProtobufValue];
   }

   function objectToFields(obj: Record<string, unknown>): { fields: Record<string, ProtobufValue> } {
     const fields: Record<string, ProtobufValue> = {};
     for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj)) {
       fields[k] = jsToProtoValue(v);
     }
     return { fields };
   }

   function jsToProtoValue(v: unknown): ProtobufValue {
     if (v === null || v === undefined) return { nullValue: 0 } as ProtobufValue;
     if (typeof v === "boolean") return { boolValue: v } as ProtobufValue;
     if (typeof v === "number") return { numberValue: v } as ProtobufValue;
     if (typeof v === "string") return { stringValue: v } as ProtobufValue;
     if (Array.isArray(v)) return { listValue: { values: v.map(jsToProtoValue) } } as ProtobufValue;
     if (typeof v === "object") return { structValue: objectToFields(v as Record<string, unknown>) } as ProtobufValue;
     return { stringValue: String(v) } as ProtobufValue;
   }
   ```
3. Run `npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui` — green (no pages changed yet).

**Acceptance**: `_util.ts` exists. Build green.

---

## Phase 1 — BTRFS Domain (Known Simple Wiring Bug)

### Task 1.1 — Create `src/grpc/plugins/btrfs.ts` Wrapper

**Requirements**: REQ-3, REQ-4.1, REQ-8

**Context**: `BtrfsPage` calls `btrfsService.getSubvolumes/getSnapshots/getSendState/getDrStatus`
against the phantom `operation.btrfs.v1.BtrfsService`. Only `getSubvolumes()` has
a genuine replacement (`list_subvolumes`); `getSnapshots`/`getSendState`/`getDrStatus`
have no real backing method — `btrfs_plugin.rs`'s `send_state`/`dr_status`/most
`snapshots` state is hand-rolled demo data, not derived from any real mechanism.
Do not wire those three to `GetState`/`stateSync.getState` as if it were live
data. Mutation methods use `pluginService.callMethod`.

**Steps**:
1. Create `crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/plugins/btrfs.ts`. Include:
   - TS types: `Subvolume`, `ListSubvolumesInput/Output`,
     `CreateSubvolumeInput`, `DeleteSubvolumeInput`, `SnapshotInput`,
     `ScrubStartInput`, `ScrubStatusInput`, `BalanceStartInput`, `BalanceStatusInput`,
     `FilesystemDfInput`, `FilesystemUsageInput`, `DeviceAddInput`, `DeviceRemoveInput`.
   - Verify field names against `btrfs_plugin.rs` method input structs.
   - Export `btrfsPlugin` service object with methods: `listSubvolumes`,
     `createSubvolume`, `deleteSubvolume`, `snapshot`, `scrubStart`, `scrubStatus`,
     `balanceStart`, `balanceStatus`, `filesystemDf`, `filesystemUsage`,
     `deviceAdd`, `deviceRemove`. All route through `pluginService.callMethod`
     with `pluginId: "btrfs"`, the method's `methodName`, and its `capabilityId`.
2. Run `npx vite build` — must be green.

**Acceptance**: File exists, no TS errors, build green.

### Task 1.2 — Wire `BtrfsPage` to `btrfsPlugin`

**Requirements**: REQ-3, REQ-4.1, REQ-6.3, REQ-8

**Context**: `BtrfsPage.tsx` imports from `@/grpc/client` (`btrfsService`) and
`@/grpc/types/btrfs`. Both are deleted after this task.

**Steps**:
1. Open `crates/op-web/ui/src/pages/BtrfsPage.tsx`.
2. Replace `import { btrfsService } from "@/grpc/client"` with
   `import { btrfsPlugin } from "@/grpc/plugins/btrfs"`.
3. Replace `import type { ... } from "@/grpc/types/btrfs"` with the
   corresponding imports from `@/grpc/plugins/btrfs`.
4. In the `load()` function inside `useEffect`: replace `getSubvolumes()` with
   `btrfsPlugin.listSubvolumes({ path: "/" })`. For `getSnapshots()`,
   `getSendState()`, `getDrStatus()`: render those panels as "not available"
   (do not substitute the plugin's demo-data fields as if they were real).
   - Map `list_subvolumes` output (array of `{name, path, uuid}`) to the
     component's `BtrfsSubvolume[]` display shape; drop or default any
     display-only fields (`purpose`, `sizeBytes`) the plugin does not return.
   - Keep the `catch` fallback to `MOCK_*` for offline development.
5. Run `npx vite build` — must be green.
6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` in `crates/op-web/ui` — must be green.

**Acceptance**: `BtrfsPage` calls no phantom service; no demo/placeholder data
is presented as live status. Build and typecheck green.

### Task 1.3 — Remove `btrfsService` from `client.ts` and `index.ts`

**Requirements**: REQ-6.3, REQ-6.4, REQ-8

**Context**: After Task 1.2, `btrfsService` has no call sites. Its import block
and the `src/grpc/types/btrfs.ts` stub can be deleted.

**Steps**:

   delete the `btrfsService` object definition.
2. In `index.ts`: delete `btrfsService` from the export list, delete
   `export * from "./types/btrfs"`, add `export * from "./plugins/btrfs"`.
3. Delete `crates/op-web/ui/src/grpc/types/btrfs.ts`.
4. Verify no remaining references: `grep -r "btrfsService\|types/btrfs" crates/op-web/ui/src/`.
5. Check proto files: if `crates/op-web/ui/proto/btrfs.proto` has zero `service`
   blocks, delete it.
6. Run `npx vite build` — green.

**Acceptance**: Zero references to `btrfsService` or `types/btrfs` in the

content.text:
I need to flag something before writing any code — I found a gap that undermines the spec's core premise.

**Finding: `PluginService.CallMethod` doesn't actually execute plugin logic for any of these six plugins.**

I traced the real call path: `pluginService.callMethod()` (client.ts) → gRPC `operation.v1.PluginService/CallMethod` → `grpc_server.rs::call_method` → `MutationEngine::mutate()`. Inside `mutate()`, only `net`/`unix_socket` plugin IDs have real dispatch arms (`mutation_engine.rs:631-699`). Every other plugin — including `btrfs`, `blockchain`, `persona`, `agent_config`, `datastore`, `cozo`, `embedding_model`, `ctl_plane_chatbot` — falls into the generic `else` branch, which for `MethodCall` does **nothing**: no dispatch, no execution. It just records an audit event and echoes the input `arguments` back as the "result."

There's a second, separate dispatch path (`dispatch_method_call`, the D-Bus `SchemaBackedInterface::call` route) that does have a `match plugin_id` executor table — but it only special-cases `rovs_commands` and `zeroclaw`; everything else there also falls to `_ => echo the input back`.

So `schema.methods.insert("create_subvolume", ...)` etc. across all six plugins are currently **pure schema/contract declarations** — real, typed, validated by the schema engine — but with no backend executor wired to actually run `btrfs subvolume create` or any real logic. Calling `list_subvolumes` today wouldn't return real subvolume data; it would just echo back whatever args you sent it, tagged `success: true`.

This means the spec's premise — "wire the UI to `PluginService.CallMethod`, it already works end to end" — is true for the *plumbing* (routing, auth, schema validation, event recording) but false for *doing anything real*. Wiring `BtrfsPage` to call these methods today would replace one broken UI (phantom service, obvious failure) with a subtly broken one (fake success, no actual effect) — arguably worse.

How do you want to proceed?

Good question to pause on — let me answer plainly, no more digging.

The **btrfs wrapper** (`src/grpc/plugins/btrfs.ts`) is just a thin translation file. Nothing more.

Right now, `BtrfsPage.tsx` calls things like `btrfsService.getSubvolumes()`, `btrfsService.createSubvolume(...)`, etc. — but `btrfsService` is fake. It points at a gRPC service (`operation.btrfs.v1.BtrfsService`) that was never actually built; the `.proto` file for it only has message definitions, no `service` block, so nothing on the backend is listening for those calls. That's the original bug.

Meanwhile, there's a real, working, generic RPC that already exists: `pluginService.callMethod({ pluginId, methodName, arguments })`. It's already wired end-to-end (routing, auth, schema lookup) and used successfully elsewhere in the app.

So the wrapper is just: **a file that gives `BtrfsPage` the same function names it already calls (`createSubvolume`, `listSubvolumes`, etc.), but each one internally calls the real `pluginService.callMethod(...)` instead of the fake `btrfsService`.** BtrfsPage's code barely changes — it swaps one import for another. No new backend code, no new Rust, no architecture — just fixing which door the UI knocks on.

The tangent I went down (whether `CallMethod` actually executes real logic once it reaches the backend) is a separate, deeper question about what happens *after* the door — and you already told me that's a known, non-blocking, platform-wide thing, not specific to btrfs. 1	//! # op-blob — schema-driven plugin object blobs
2	//!
3	//! Implements the pipeline defined in
4	//! `.kiro/specs/schemars-to-reflection-plugin-pipeline/` and the
5	//! schema-coupled-plugin-blob-reflection whitepaper:
6	//!
7	//! ```text
8	//! Rust state/input/output structs (#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)])
9	//!   -> schemars JSON Schema 2020-12
10	//!   -> adapter::plugin_schema_from_json
11	//!   -> PluginSchema                      <- SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH
12	//!   -> blob::blobify
13	//!   -> PluginObjectBlob                  <- sealed projection: schema + metadata
14	//!        schema_json + schema_hash
15	//!        D-Bus identity (/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>)
16	//!        gRPC identity + FileDescriptorSet (typed, per-method)
17	//!        method manifest (subid, capability, side_effect, idempotent)
18	//!   -> catalog::ActiveReflectionCatalog  <- /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<id>.<hash>.blob
19	//!   -> btrfs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image <- btrfs filesystem in the blob artifact
20	//! ```
21	//!
22	//! Non-negotiable rules carried over from the whitepaper:
23	//! 1. `PluginSchema` is the source of truth. The blob is a frozen projection,
24	//!    never a second source.
25	//! 2. The plugin owns its schema; schemars is the derivation tool, not the
26	//!    published contract.
27	//! 3. Blobs are per-object artifacts (one plugin, one blob, one schema hash),
28	//!    replacing the monolithic `/dev/shm/live-schema.json` runtime shape.
29	//! 4. Reflection advertises only active blobs; descriptors are synthesized
30	//!    from `MethodDecl.args/returns` — no phantom services.
31	//! 5. Zero-copy: a sealed blob is a sectioned byte image; `BlobRef` hands out
32	//!    borrowed slices (schema JSON, manifest, descriptor bytes) without
33	//!    re-parsing or re-allocating on the read path.
34	//!
35	//! Divergences from the full workspace (documented, deliberate):
36	//! - The local `PluginSchema` is a reduced WORKING VIEW used only for
37	//!   descriptor/manifest synthesis. Real plugins are sealed through
38	//!   `blobify_plugin_schema`, which seals the FULL canonical
39	//!   `op_state_store::PluginSchema` JSON (signals, guarantees, category, …);
40	//!   read it back with `BlobRef::state_store_schema`.
41	//! - Descriptor bytes are hand-encoded protobuf (`descriptor.rs`) instead of
42	//!   prost — keeps the crate dependency-free per NFR-3's spirit.

72	    plugin_id: &str,

74	) -> PluginObjectBlob {
75	    blobify_plugin_schema_with_identity(plugin_id, schema, None)

78	/// Seal the FULL canonical workspace schema. The sealed SCHEMA_JSON section
79	/// (and the schema hash) is the complete `op_state_store::PluginSchema` —
80	/// signals, guarantees, category and all. The reduced local `PluginSchema` is
81	/// derived from the same canonical value purely as the working view for
82	/// descriptor/manifest synthesis; it is never what gets sealed.
83	pub fn blobify_plugin_schema_with_identity(
84	    plugin_id: &str,
85	    mut schema: op_state_store::PluginSchema,
86	    identity: Option<BlobIdentity>,
87	) -> PluginObjectBlob {
88	    schema.name = blob::canonical_plugin_id(plugin_id);
89	    let canonical_value =
90	        serde_json::to_value(&schema).expect("op-state-store PluginSchema serializes");
91	    // serde_json's Map is BTreeMap-backed (no `preserve_order`), so this is
92	    // deterministic key-sorted canonical JSON.
93	    let canonical_json =
94	        serde_json::to_string(&canonical_value).expect("canonical value serializes");
95	    let working: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(canonical_value)
96	        .expect("op-blob PluginSchema view accepts op-state-store schema");
97	    blob::blobify_canonical(&working, canonical_json, identity)
98	}

Good challenge — you're right, sealing to scratch doesn't make anything live. Let me be precise about what's actually persistent vs. not:

- **Persistent already**: my edit to `btrfs_plugin.rs` (the Rust source). That's a real, permanent fix, checked into the working tree — the schema function will produce the correct output types every time it runs, forever, regardless of any blob state.
- **Not yet persistent**: the actual sealed `.blob` file sitting in `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/btrfs.*.blob` right now was sealed *before* my fix, so it still has the old `AckOutput`-only schema. `/dev/shm` is tmpfs — it doesn't pick up source changes on its own; something has to re-run the sealer against the new binary.

Sealing into scratch was me being overly cautious about touching the live system's shared directory while other processes might depend on its current contents — but you're right that it only proves the fix *works*, it doesn't make it *effective*. To actually make the live catalog reflect this fix, `opblob seal-shm` needs to run against `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs` for real (or however this system normally reseals on deploy/restart, per the s6 service that runs it at boot).

1	//! Generic, provider-agnostic embedding-model plugin.
2	//!
3	//! The single EMBEDDING surface — provider, model id, endpoint, and the shared
4	//! output dimensionality. The model is a FIELD, not the plugin's identity: swap
5	//! `voyage-4` → `voyage-4-lite` (or an Ollama/local embedder) by changing
6	//! `model_id`. This is the ONLY plugin that knows how to reach an embedding

8	//! delegate here and embed no model of their own. It is the embedding sibling of

content.content:
# Voyage AI Text Embedding API Reference

## Endpoint
**POST** `https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings`

## Request Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `input` | string \| array | Yes | — | Single text or list of texts (max 1,000 items). Token limits: 1M for lite models; 320K for standard/v2; 120K for large/specialized. |
| `model` | string | Yes | — | Model name: `voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4`, `voyage-4-lite`, `voyage-3-large`, `voyage-3.5`, `voyage-3.5-lite`, `voyage-code-3`, `voyage-finance-2`, `voyage-law-2` |
| `input_type` | string \| null | No | null | Options: `null`, `query`, `document`. When set, prepends retrieval-specific prompts before vectorization. |
| `truncation` | boolean | No | true | If true, truncates over-length inputs; if false, raises error. |
| `output_dimension` | integer \| null | No | null | Supported values for most models: 2048, 1024 (default), 512, 256. |
| `output_dtype` | string | No | float | Options: `float`, `int8`, `uint8`, `binary`, `ubinary`. Support varies by model. |
| `encoding_format` | string \| null | No | null | Options: `null`, `base64`. Specifies embedding encoding. |

## Response Schema
- **200 Success**: Returns list of embeddings (format depends on `output_dtype` and `encoding_format`)
- **4XX Client Error**: Request format or rate limit issue
- **5XX Server Error**: High traffic or server issue

## Models
Recommended: `voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4`, `voyage-4-lite`, `voyage-3-large`, `voyage-3.5`, `voyage-3.5-lite`, `voyage-code-3`, `voyage-finance-2`, `voyage-law-2`

**Note**: Complete response schema structure, individual error codes, and rate limits are not provided in the source documentation.

Here's the fuller structured data from the official API reference (docs.voyageai.com/reference/embeddings-api):

**Endpoint**: `POST https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings`

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | string \| array | Yes | — | Single text or list (max 1,000 items). Token budget per request: 1M for lite models; 320K for standard/v2 models; 120K for large/specialized models |
| `model` | string | Yes | — | `voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4`, `voyage-4-lite`, `voyage-3-large`, `voyage-3.5`, `voyage-3.5-lite`, `voyage-code-3`, `voyage-finance-2`, `voyage-law-2` |
| `input_type` | string\|null | No | null | `null`, `query`, `document` — prepends retrieval-specific prompt when set |
| `truncation` | boolean | No | true | If false, over-length input raises an error instead of truncating |
| `output_dimension` | integer\|null | No | null (→1024) | 2048, 1024 (default), 512, 256 |
| `output_dtype` | string | No | `float` | `float`, `int8`, `uint8`, `binary`, `ubinary` — support varies by model |
| `encoding_format` | string\|null | No | null | `null`, `base64` |

Excellent — now I have the **exact, official OpenAPI schema** (openapi 3.0.2) from `github.com/voyage-ai/openapi/voyage-openapi.yml`. Full request/response shape for `POST /embeddings`:

**Request body** (`required: [input, model]`)
| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | `string` \| `array<string>` | — | max 128 items; token budget: 1M (`voyage-3-lite`), 320K (`voyage-3`/`voyage-2`), 120K (`voyage-3-large`, `voyage-code-3`, `voyage-large-2-instruct`, `voyage-finance-2`, `voyage-multilingual-2`, `voyage-law-2`, `voyage-large-2`) |
| `model` | `string` | — | required |
| `input_type` | `enum[null,query,document]` | `null` | prepends a retrieval prompt when set |
| `truncation` | `boolean` | `true` | if `false`, over-length input raises an error instead |
| `output_dimension` | `integer\|null` | `null` | only `voyage-3-large`/`voyage-code-3` support 2048/1024(default)/512/256; other models have one fixed dim |
| `output_dtype` | `enum[float,int8,uint8,binary,ubinary]` | `float` | int8/uint8/binary/ubinary only on `voyage-3-large`/`voyage-code-3` |
| `encoding_format` | `enum[null,base64]` | `null` | base64-encodes the NumPy array |

**Response 200**
```
{
  object: string ("list"),
  data: [{ object: string ("embedding"), embedding: number[], index: integer }],
  model: string,
  usage: { total_tokens: integer }
}
```
**4XX**: `{ detail: string }`. **5XX**: no body schema given.

**General-purpose — Voyage 3 (previous)**
- `voyage-3-large` — 32K ctx, dims 256/512/1024/2048, all input types, all dtypes
- `voyage-3.5`, `voyage-3.5-lite` — 32K ctx, dims 256/512/1024/2048, all input types, **float only**
- `voyage-3` — 32K ctx, 1024 dims fixed, float only
- `voyage-3-lite` — 32K ctx, 512 dims fixed, float only

**Legacy/deprecated**
- `voyage-large-2` — 16K ctx, 1536 dims, float only
- `voyage-large-2-instruct` — 16K ctx, 1024 dims, float only
- `voyage-2`, `voyage-lite-02-instruct`[dep], `voyage-02`[dep], `voyage-01`[dep], `voyage-lite-01`[dep], `voyage-lite-01-instruct`[dep] — 4K ctx, 1024 dims, float only

**Code-specialized**
- `voyage-code-3` (current) — 32K ctx, dims 256/512/1024/2048, all dtypes
- `voyage-code-2` (legacy) — 16K ctx, 1536 dims, float only

**Legal-specialized**
- `voyage-law-2` — 16K ctx, 1024 dims, float only

**Finance-specialized**
- `voyage-finance-2` — 32K ctx, 1024 dims, float only

**Multilingual-specialized**
- `voyage-multilingual-2` — 32K ctx, 1024 dims, float only

**Open-weight**
- `voyage-4-nano` — 32K ctx, dims 256/512/1024/2048, all dtypes

Note this reconciles the earlier discrepancy: the docs site treats `voyage-4-large/4/4-lite` as current-gen (matches this codebase's `VoyageModel` enum), while the GitHub `voyage-openapi.yml` (v1.1) still recommends the voyage-3 family — the OpenAPI repo is stale relative to the live docs.

Ready to build `ModelSpec`/`EmbedInput`/`EmbedOutput` in `embedding_model.rs` against this full picture? Given the breadth (9+ families, per-model dtype/dim variability), I'd suggest scoping the Rust schema to just the fields this plugin actually needs to expose (family, context length, supported dims, supported dtypes, current vs legacy status) rather than hardcoding all ~20 model IDs — want me to proceed on that basis, or do you want the full model catalog embedded as static data in the plugin?

That settles it. Cross-checking all three sources:

- **`voyage-openapi.yml`** (OpenAPI spec, updated May 2026): authoritative for the **exact wire schema** — field names, types, enums (`input`, `model`, `input_type`, `truncation`, `output_dimension`, `output_dtype`, `encoding_format`; response `{object, data[{object,embedding,index}], model, usage.total_tokens}`).
- **`voyageai-python`** (Official Python client, updated **2026-07-01** — most recent of all repos): confirms the same field names in the real `Client.embed()` signature (`texts, model, input_type, truncation, output_dtype, output_dimension`) and response object (`EmbeddingsObject{embeddings, total_tokens}`). But its hardcoded fallback `VOYAGE_EMBED_DEFAULT_MODEL = "voyage-2"` is **stale/legacy** — it's just a deprecated-with-warning fallback for callers who omit `model`, not a recommendation. Also reveals two more real API surfaces beyond plain embed: `contextualized_embed` (chunked/contextualized embeddings) and multimodal/reranking objects — out of scope for this plugin, but worth knowing they exist.
- **`docs.voyageai.com/docs/embeddings`**: the only source with the **exhaustive, current model catalog** (voyage-4 family as current-gen, full family breakdown, deprecation flags).

input.description: Check if contextualized_embedding has its own endpoint

content.text:
Direct answer: **the official Python client (`voyageai-python`) has more complete method coverage than the OpenAPI spec** — and it's stale in the other direction: the OpenAPI spec is missing a whole endpoint.

**OpenAPI spec** (`voyage-openapi.yml`) — 3 endpoints:
- `/embeddings`
- `/multimodalembeddings`
- `/rerank`

**Python client** (`voyageai-python`, api_resources/) — **4** method surfaces:
- `embedding.py` → `/embeddings`
- `multimodal_embedding.py` → `/multimodalembeddings`
- `reranking.py` → `/rerank`
- **`contextualized_embedding.py`** → object name `contextualizedembeddings` — **a real endpoint not in the OpenAPI spec at all**. It's `Client.contextualized_embed()` (chunked/contextualized embeddings, with auto-chunking support), and its params largely mirror `embed` (`inputs`, `model`, `input_type`, `output_dtype`, `output_dimension`, plus `chunk_fn`/`enable_auto_chunking`/`chunk_size`/`chunk_overlap`).

So for parameter-level accuracy on the plain `embed` method, both sources agree (which is what I built `EmbedInput`/`EmbedOutput` from). But if you want full method coverage for this plugin, there are three more real capabilities not modeled yet: `contextualized_embed`, `multimodal_embed`, `rerank`.

Do you want me to scope `embedding_model`'s schema to just `embed`/`list_models`/`get_config`/`set_model`/`update_config`/`get_stats` (current plan), or add methods for contextualized/multimodal/rerank too?

message.content: all of them

The first 200 million tokens for voyage-4-large, voyage-4, voyage-4-lite, voyage-context-3, and voyage-code-3, or the first 50 million tokens for voyage-multilingual-2, voyage-finance-2, voyage-law-2, and voyage-code-2, are free for every account.

content.text:
The six phantom frontend gRPC services (from the `.kiro/specs/phantom-services-to-plugins/` spec) — each references a service with no real backend, since their `.proto` files have message definitions only, no `service` block:

1. **`operation.accountability.v1` `ChatbotAccountabilityService`** → maps to the real `ctl_plane_chatbot` plugin
2. **`operation.blockchain.v1` `BlockchainService`** → maps to the real `blockchain` plugin
3. **`operation.btrfs.v1` `BtrfsService`** → maps to the real `btrfs` plugin (this is the one we did the most backend work on)
4. **`operation.agent.persona.v1` `PersonaService`** → maps to `persona` + `agent_config` plugins
5. **`operation.datastore.v1` `DataStoreService`** → maps to `datastore` + `cozo` (+ `memory`, `qdrant`) plugins
6. **`operation.embedding.v1` `EmbeddingService`** → maps to `embedding_model` (+ `qdrant`) plugin

The fix direction (per the spec, and per your "we only work on backend" correction): the UI should call these existing plugins via `PluginService.CallMethod`, not through new proto services — that wiring itself is Lovable's job. My work has been strictly backend: correcting the schemas of the plugins these phantom services should route to (`btrfs`, `ctl_plane_chatbot`, `embedding_model`, and now `cozo` for the datastore domain), so their methods actually declare real typed data instead of generic `AckOutput` placeholders.

nothing we have to do during tthe seal process or fix somme other area to comjmlyu?
  Blocker 2 — three parallel descriptor generators (the one-schema violation). Besides op-blob's,
  op-grpc-bridge re-synthesizes descriptors from PluginSchema via prost
  (per_plugin_reflection.rs::generate_method_file_descriptor_proto, frozen in plugin_grpc_gen.rs:147), and
  build.rs generates a third set. Per OD-32, nothing reads the blob's sealed section. The bridge should
  hydrate its reflection catalog from blob section 3 and delete its own synthesis — otherwise UI codegen has
  two candidate sources and you're back to drift.

  Blocker 3 — OD-32 sealing gaps land first. Sealing currently drops schema fields (signals, guarantees,
  etc.), there are two blob-dir writers, and no dir manifest/commit point. Generate UI types from the blob
  before that's fixed and the UI inherits the truncated schema.

  One design caveat worth internalizing: the JSON-Schema→proto walk is intentionally lossy — enums,
  multi-branch unions, and free-form objects degrade to JSON-encoded strings; all integers widen to int64;
  and no proto3_optional flag is emitted, so Option<scalar> presence is lost (unset vs 0 are
  indistinguishable on the wire). That's acceptable for transport but wrong as a form-rendering source. So
  the split should be: SCHEMA_JSON (section 1) drives UI rendering (json_render path — enums, constraints,
  descriptions survive there), DESCRIPTOR_SET drives wire typing only.

  Recommended order: (1) bridge reads blob descriptors + mounts typed services, deleting its duplicate
  synthesis; (2) an obs.* export command dumps the catalog descriptor set; (3) repoint proto:gen at
  --descriptor_set_in; (4) hash-pin + runtime drift check; (5) delete the hand-maintained protos — including
  the six for services that should be plugins anyway. Full findings appended to SIGNALS.md under OD-32.

Confirmed — this is a real, live risk right now, not hypothetical. Both **`op-grpc-bridge`** (PID 28939, running since Jul04) and **`op-web-server`** (PID 5496, running since 17:55 today) are live and were built **before** tonight's schema changes. Two consequences:

1. **The live gRPC reflection surface doesn't see any of tonight's fixes yet** — `op-grpc-bridge`'s in-process `per_plugin_reflection.rs` synthesis runs from its currently-loaded (old) binary, completely independent of the blob I just resealed.
2. **Clobber risk**: per the "two writers" finding, `grpc_server::register_plugin_methods` (inside `op-grpc-bridge`) also writes to `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs` at runtime on plugin registration. If that old-binary process re-registers `btrfs`/`cozo`/`ctl_plane_chatbot`/`embedding_model` for any reason (restart, reconnect, etc.) before it's rebuilt, it will write the **old, pre-fix schema** right back over the fresh reseal I just did.

To make tonight's fixes actually durable and live (not just "correct in a blob nobody's serving yet"), the running binaries need to be rebuilt against the updated `op-plugins` crate and restarted via `s6d`. That's a live-service-affecting action, so I want to confirm before doing it rather than assume — want me to rebuild and restart `op-grpc-bridge`/`op-web-server`/`opdbus` now?

#!/bin/sh
exec 2>&1
# opdbus - hypervisor WireGuard identity tunnel to Oracle VPS (wg0, 10.0.0.2 <-> 10.0.0.1)
# Gateway IP and iptables are managed by ovsbr0-init
IFACE="wg0"

if ! wg show "${IFACE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wg-quick up "${IFACE}"
fi

# Add routes manually (Table=off means wg-quick won't add them)
ip route replace 10.0.0.0/24 dev "${IFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true
ip route replace 10.0.0.1/32 dev "${IFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true

exec sleep infinity
--- op-web-srv run ---
#!/bin/sh
# op-web-server — unified HTTP API + embedded UI for op-dbus
export PORT="${PORT:-8080}"
[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment
export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS
: "${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:?DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS must be set in /etc/op-dbus/environment}"
export OP_DBUS_GRPC_ADDR="${OP_DBUS_GRPC_ADDR:-http://10.200.0.1:50051}"
export OP_DBUS_ADDR="${OP_DBUS_ADDR:-$OP_DBUS_GRPC_ADDR}"
export OP_MEMORY_DB="${OP_MEMORY_DB:-/var/lib/op-dbus/cognitive.db}"
export OP_WEB_STATIC_DIR="${OP_WEB_STATIC_DIR:-/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/crates/op-web/ui/dist}"
export RUST_LOG="${RUST_LOG:-op_web=info,info}"
exec s6-setuidgid jeremy /usr/local/bin/op-web-server

#!/bin/sh
exec 2>&1
# opdbus - hypervisor WireGuard identity tunnel to Oracle VPS (wg0, 10.0.0.2 <-> 10.0.0.1)
# Gateway IP and iptables are managed by ovsbr0-init
IFACE="wg0"

if ! wg show "${IFACE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wg-quick up "${IFACE}"
fi

# Add routes manually (Table=off means wg-quick won't add them)
ip route replace 10.0.0.0/24 dev "${IFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true
ip route replace 10.0.0.1/32 dev "${IFACE}" 2>/dev/null || true

exec sleep infinity

: "${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:?DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS must be set in /etc/op-dbus/environment}"
